dimensions.name: Contract & environment reconnaissance

evidence.note: First actions opened helpers.py AND run.sh together; agent explicitly states the wire contract is 'defined by /dev_tests/helpers.py rather than the prose alone,' extracting REST paths, request bodies, and the workbooks listing envelope.

Systematically read every public test file (api, engine, deps, spill, copy_fill, sort_filter, csv, xlsx, ooxml, xlsx_oracle, pivot, locale, validation, iter, collab), pinning down cell kinds incl. spill ghosts, spill_range shape, error names, ghost-write 400, and LWW-by-seq before coding.

Probed installed libraries (fastapi/uvicorn/openpyxl/websockets/numpy/scipy/formulas/xlcalculator) and the /app/data scaffold; the empty-env result directly drove the custom-engine + install-in-start.sh approach.

During XLSX debugging, empirically inspected exported OOXML XML against openpyxl(data_only=True) and reasoned about openpyxl's relationship attribute ordering — a living, evidence-based model of the readability constraint rather than assumption.

Proactively hardened contract corners the smoke suite doesn't exercise (multi-array MAP, BYCOL, OFFSET, deep chains) to avoid passing only the exact public cases — anticipating hidden-suite variation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent meets the level-8 anchor comprehensively: it systematically extracted the full contract from helpers.py and all public tests (kinds, spill ghosts, spill_range, error names, envelope), cross-referenced against prose, and probed installed libraries before choosing an approach. It also shows genuine level-10 behavior — empirically probing openpyxl OOXML readability when the XLSX path broke, reasoning about underspecified semantics from authoritative behavior, and proactively identifying hidden-suite corners. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because reconnaissance was front-loaded rather than a continuous per-feature re-consultation of helpers.py, so I place it at 9.

dimensions.name: Layering a vast surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Establishes foundations-first sequencing: inspect workspace and match the /dev_tests/helpers.py contract, then read visible tests to pin request/response shapes before building — a dependency-respecting opening.

Surveys the whole surface (formulas, arrays, propagation, CSV/XLSX, collab, formats, pivots, locale, validation, iterative calc) and sequences service entrypoint + dependency bootstrap + foreground server first, before the app — foundations before features.

Builds the core as one monolithic module then plans to run the visible suite 'in slices' to catch contract/evaluator defects — a rough done-check gate, but not milestone-gated incremental construction.

Phase progression with rough completion criteria: 'base API and formula corpus passing → moving to stateful behavior (cycles, spill, fill, sort/filter, import/export)' then 'all visible tests passing → hardening pass.' Later features deferred until earlier phases pass.

Final phase adds an explicit restart/persistence done-check ('manual restart check for persisted state') and full-suite rerun — verification gates exist per phase but were never enumerated as an upfront milestone map with per-item done criteria.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent follows a sensible, dependency-aware order — contract recon → bootable server/health/persistence → core cell model+engine → stateful behaviors → hardening → restart check — with rough per-phase done-checks (suite slices, all-visible-passing, restart persistence), which clearly exceeds the flat undifferentiated list of anchor 3 and satisfies anchor 5's 'foundations first with rough milestones.' It falls short of anchor 8 because the decomposition is a rolling post-hoc narrative rather than an explicit milestone hierarchy where each piece names its confirmation up front, the build was one monolithic module rather than incrementally gated, and cross-cutting invariants (e.g. WebSocket cells == REST patch shape) were never called out as shared milestones. That places it between 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness checks beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Ran the /dev_tests smoke suite in slices and then in full (131 passed); this is the baseline green-suite check, and reruns after fixes (69, 75) confirm it's the primary verification loop.
Genuine persistence-after-restart check: created a formula workbook, killed and restarted the process, then re-read B1=42 to confirm state survived — a real independent check beyond run.sh.
Spot verifications: health endpoint via curl, DELETE returns 204, and direct inspection of /app/data/state.json contents — modest own checks.
A couple of core-formula spot-checks (IFNA result) after adding functions — targeted but ad hoc, not a systematic per-function-family Excel oracle.

XLSX/ooxml/oracle suites are only exercised via run.sh; the agent never re-opens its own exports with openpyxl to confirm named ranges/formats/styles/CF survive, and never runs perf-budget or spill/#CIRC! adversarial checks of its own.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treats the smoke suite as the backbone but supplements it with a handful of its own checks — a rigorous multi-cycle persistence-after-restart test, the health endpoint, state-file inspection, and a few core-formula spot-checks — which matches anchor 5 almost exactly. It does not reach 8: there is no independent validation of XLSX round-trip via openpyxl re-open, no explicit perf-budget testing, and no self-built spill/#SPILL!/#CIRC!/goal-seek edge-case corpus, all of which the hidden suite emphasizes.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge feature matrix

evidence.note: Read the entire visible test suite file-by-file before building, forming an explicit inventory of the feature surface (step 27 enumerates 'formulas, dynamic arrays, dependency propagation, CSV/XLSX, collaboration, formats, pivots, locale, validation, iterative calc') — an accurate up-front picture of what must be tracked.

Ran the visible suite in slices and narrated state transitions as pieces landed: 'base API and public formula corpus are passing' (39), 'All visible tests are passing' (42). Milestone-level status tracking, but narrated in prose rather than a persistent granular checklist.

After the hardening edits (43-52) it re-ran the FULL visible suite (131 passed) specifically to catch regressions from the new code — a hallmark 8-anchor behavior of re-verifying prior work as new code lands.

Manual probe found a real gap — =IFNA(NA(),"x") returned #NAME? (unimplemented) at 72 — then fixed it (73) and re-verified it returned 'x' (78). Caught a gap beyond the suite and closed the loop, not a premature 'finished' declaration.

Persistence/restart probes and targeted re-runs of test slices after later fixes (69, 75) show ongoing verification of specific subsystems rather than assuming done. However tracking stays coarse; no granular done/partial/failing matrix and little debugging occurred, so no demonstration of detecting thrashing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a coherent, updated picture of the feature surface: it inventories the whole suite up front, narrates status as milestones land, and — crucially — re-runs the full suite after hardening (57) and targeted slices after later fixes (69, 75) to catch regressions, plus finds and closes a real gap (IFNA, 72-78) before wrapping. This clears the level-5 anchor and reaches into the level-8 're-run prior checks to catch regressions' trait. It falls short of 8/10 because status is tracked as coarse prose milestones rather than a live granular done/partial/failing matrix, and because the smooth first-pass test results gave little occasion to demonstrate detecting stuck/circular debugging or budgeting effort against uncovered surface. Level 6 fits: solidly above a working checklist, with genuine regression-catching, but not the horizon-wide granular reconciliation of the top anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when semantics or perf diverge

evidence.note: First full suite surfaced 10 failures; agent diagnosed each to a distinct real cause (tuple flattening, #N/A classification, error-inspecting predicates, LET-lambda dispatch, WebSocket support, iterative-calc stop) instead of symptom-patching — root-cause fixing per feature (anchor 5).

Recognized WebSocket failure as a missing upgrade/library capability, fixed the dependency in start.sh, restarted, and re-verified the previously-failing subset before a full rerun — targeted diagnosis + re-verification.

Own custom check (not in smoke suite) revealed openpyxl(data_only=True) couldn't read cached values. Agent iterated through two separate root causes — absolute /xl/ rel targets + empty <v/>, then relationship attribute ordering — re-checking after each restart until it passed. Reworking the OOXML approach when openpyxl couldn't read the export (anchor 8 example).
Preemptively raised recursion ceiling so long formula chains don't fail topo traversal — smaller adaptation to anticipated hidden-suite stress.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the whole arc the agent reliably diagnosed and fixed the true cause of each failing feature and re-verified (anchor 5), and in the XLSX/openpyxl episode it treated a surprising read failure as a signal about its OOXML export approach, iterating through two distinct root causes with restart-and-recheck loops until the export became openpyxl-readable — the anchor-8 example. It stops short of 8+ because corrections were within-approach patches rather than a decisive re-architecture and no foundational assumption was overturned early, placing it at a solid 7 between anchors 5 and 8.

dimensions.name: Coverage-maximizing effort allocation

evidence.note: Opening strategy: build the smallest complete implementation matching the client's calls, then 'expand where the hidden requirements are likely to probe' — an explicit breadth-first-then-deepen plan.
Chose a proper AST evaluator over string-eval because it's the shared enabler for spills/LET/LAMBDA/ranges/errors — investing in a foundation that unlocks broad coverage cheaply.

Single broad build: ~160+ functions across every catalog family plus locale translations, and all endpoints (collab, pivots, goal seek, validation, conditional formatting, names, CSV/XLSX). Locks in wide end-to-end coverage before perfecting any corner.
Post-run triage patches 'concentrated and mechanical' failures rather than over-investing in one area — proportionate effort.
Explicit depth pass on 'areas the hidden suite is likely to vary' (deep chains, multi-array MAP, BYCOL, OFFSET) — a breadth-vs-depth call tied to expected graded weight.

Deepened high-value/high-risk areas: perf chain, persistence-across-restart, and XLSX cached-value openpyxl round-trip (a graded corpus). Depth directed to likely-graded surfaces, though the XLSX fix was pursued to completion without an explicit payoff time-box.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent secured broad end-to-end coverage of the huge function catalog and endpoint surface first (steps 25-28), then made explicit, payoff-aware depth choices — hardening high-variance formula areas and high-value graded surfaces like XLSX round-trip and persistence (steps 56, 64-87). This is precisely the level-8 pattern: explicit breadth-vs-depth calls tied to likely graded weight, breadth locked in early, then deepening high-value/high-risk areas. It falls short of 10 because there is little evidence of iteratively revisiting the allocation or consciously cutting/deferring low-yield perfectionism (e.g., the XLSX fix was carried to completion without a stated marginal-value tradeoff).

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a from-scratch Excel-clone product (persistent server + REST + WebSocket collab + vanilla SPA + a 100+ function Excel-365 formula engine with dynamic-array spilling, dependency-graph dirty recompute under perf budgets, XLSX/CSV round-trip against a held-out LibreOffice oracle, plus pivots, defined names, conditional formatting, locale input, validation, iterative calc, and goal seek). The exact wire contract is deliberately under-specified in prose and must be reverse-engineered from the first-party client at /dev_tests/helpers.py, and grading is a large HIDDEN suite. This task warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension: deep contract orientation, layered milestones over a vast surface, self-built verification against Excel semantics, continuous progress tracking, and constant course-correction — plus strategic allocation of finite effort across breadth vs. depth.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reverse-engineering the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and probing the environment (available libs, run.sh, Excel/LibreOffice semantics) before and while building, instead of guessing the API from prose.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly says the true wire contract (ids, cell shapes, patch/fill/sort/filter bodies, kind discriminator, spill fields, listing envelope) is 'whatever helpers.py already calls into.' Guessing instead of reading it guarantees systematic mismatch with the hidden suite; the prose alone is insufficient.

anchors.0: Starts implementing endpoints purely from the prose; never opens helpers.py or run.sh; invents field names.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once for a couple of endpoints, then builds mostly from prose; misses the discriminator/spill/envelope details.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py to pin down the core cell/workbook/patch shapes and runs run.sh early to see what the smoke suite expects before coding those paths.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the full contract from helpers.py (every request body, cell kind incl. spill ghosts, spill_range, error names, listing envelope), cross-references it against prose to resolve ambiguities, and probes the environment (installed libraries for OOXML/formula I/O, openpyxl readability constraints) before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Maintains a living, evidence-based model of the contract: re-consults helpers.py whenever a new feature surface is touched, infers underspecified Excel semantics (spill/#SPILL!, criteria wildcards, LWW-by-seq, locale canonicalization) from authoritative reasoning rather than assumption, and proactively identifies contract corners the smoke suite doesn't exercise but the hidden suite likely will.

dimensions.name: Layering a vast surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the enormous feature surface into an ordered dependency-respecting hierarchy (bootable server+health+persistence → cell model → dependency/recompute → formula engine → dynamic arrays/spill → I/O → collab → SPA → analyst surface → iterative/goal-seek), each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With dozens of interdependent subsystems and hard foundations (persistence, dependency graph) that everything else builds on, an undifferentiated push collapses. Sequencing and per-milestone done-criteria are what keep the build coherent over a very long horizon.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random features (e.g. pivots before the cell model works); no notion of 'done' per piece.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do list that ignores dependencies and lacks per-item completion criteria.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan that establishes foundations first (bootable server, health, persistence, core cell CRUD) before layering features, with rough milestones.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each milestone names how it will be confirmed done (e.g. 'recompute topo-order verified on a 3-cell chain before adding functions'), and later features are deliberately deferred until their prerequisites pass.
anchors.10: A milestone structure that also encodes risk and coupling: foundational/high-leverage subsystems (dep graph, spill materialization, XLSX round-trip) are sequenced first and gated by concrete checks, cross-cutting invariants (WebSocket cells payload == REST patch shape) are called out as shared milestones, and the plan is revised as real dependencies surface rather than followed rigidly.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness checks beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks that go past the non-exhaustive /dev_tests suite: validating formula results against known Excel semantics, exercising spill/#CIRC!/error propagation, confirming XLSX openpyxl-readability and value round-trip, and testing perf budgets and persistence-across-restart.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec warns the smoke suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a hidden suite with a LibreOffice ground-truth oracle. Assuming 'run.sh passes' means correct is the dominant failure mode; correctness of 100+ functions and round-trips must be independently established.

anchors.0: No verification, or only eyeballing; never runs run.sh.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh and treats a green smoke suite as proof of correctness; no independent checks of function values or edge cases.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite plus a handful of own spot-checks on core formulas, persistence-after-restart, and the health endpoint.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks the smoke suite doesn't cover: representative formulas per function family validated against known-correct Excel outputs, spill/#SPILL!/#CIRC! and error-propagation cases, XLSX exports re-opened with openpyxl to confirm named ranges/formats/styles/CF survive, and explicit perf checks against the stated budgets.
anchors.10: Establishes an independent correctness oracle and uses it systematically — e.g. cross-checking evaluated values against real Excel/LibreOffice reasoning across many functions and locales, round-trip differential tests (export→import→compare, REST-vs-WebSocket payload parity), adversarial edge cases (occupied spill targets, iterative-calc convergence, goal-seek non-convergence), and treats any discrepancy as a signal to dig rather than a nuisance — verification depth scales with the breadth of the surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge feature matrix
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which of the many subsystems/functions are implemented, working, or broken, and detecting stuck/circular states (e.g. repeatedly re-debugging one formula) across a very long build.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large enough that it's easy to lose the plot — believe a feature is done when it regressed, or sink disproportionate time into one function while dozens go untouched. Accurate status tracking is what sustains progress to the finish.

anchors.0: No sense of overall state; forgets whole feature areas; no detection of being stuck.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; rediscovers unfinished areas late; keeps retrying the same failing approach without noticing.
anchors.5: Keeps a working checklist of major features and updates it as pieces land, catching obvious gaps before wrapping up.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular status of subsystems and function families (done / partial / failing), re-runs prior checks to catch regressions as new code lands, and notices when it's thrashing on one problem to redirect effort.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate horizon-wide picture that drives decisions: explicitly reconciles claimed-done against re-verified-done, detects circular debugging early and changes tactic, budgets remaining effort against the still-uncovered surface, and avoids both premature 'finished' declarations and rabbit-holes.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when semantics or perf diverge
dimensions.description: Revising design, approach, or library choices when reality contradicts assumptions — Excel-semantics mismatches, spill/dependency bugs, perf-budget misses, or XLSX/openpyxl incompatibilities — rather than pressing on with a falsified plan.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many parts are subtle (dynamic-array spilling, dirty-only topo recompute under tight budgets, iterative fixed-point calc, OOXML that stays openpyxl-readable). First designs will be wrong somewhere; the ability to detect and re-architect is what separates a working product from a stuck one.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps a broken approach; ships on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Makes only local patches around symptoms (e.g. special-casing one failing formula) without questioning the underlying design.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and fixes the real cause for that feature, and adjusts nearby plans accordingly.
anchors.8: Treats surprising failures as signals about the design: e.g. reworks the recompute/dependency model when perf budgets are missed, or the chosen OOXML approach when openpyxl can't read the export, and updates the plan to reflect the new understanding.
anchors.10: Repeatedly and cheaply re-architects when warranted: recognizes a foundational assumption is wrong early (before it contaminates dependent features), weighs alternative strategies against evidence, migrates approach decisively, and re-verifies the affected surface — converting divergence into durable design improvements rather than accumulating hacks.

dimensions.name: Coverage-maximizing effort allocation
dimensions.description: Strategically allocating finite effort across a surface far larger than can be perfected, to maximize expected hidden-suite coverage — trading breadth (many function families / endpoints minimally working) against depth (a few done flawlessly).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The catalog and feature list are enormous and grading is a broad hidden suite; a practitioner who perfects one corner while leaving whole families unimplemented scores worse than one who gets broad coverage working and then deepens high-value areas. This portfolio judgment is specific to this task's structure and isn't captured by sequencing alone.

anchors.0: Pours all effort into one narrow area (e.g. perfecting pivots) leaving most of the surface unimplemented, or spreads so thin nothing works end-to-end.
anchors.3: Follows the spec top-to-bottom without regard to payoff, running out of horizon with large high-value areas untouched.
anchors.5: Consciously prioritizes getting core, high-frequency surface working broadly before niche features, giving reasonable coverage.
anchors.8: Makes explicit breadth-vs-depth calls tied to likely graded weight — securing broad end-to-end coverage of common functions/endpoints first, then deepening high-value or high-risk areas — and consciously time-boxes low-payoff rabbit holes.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, evidence-informed portfolio: estimates where hidden-suite value concentrates, sequences to lock in broad coverage early, revisits allocation as time is spent, and cuts or defers low-yield perfectionism to redirect effort toward the highest marginal coverage — maximizing graded outcome under the horizon constraint.
